attribution_limitations: The discussion states the scrotal lymphedema was "probably caused by radiotherapy" and that liquid silicone was "also a contributory factor". The cause is hedged and is not recorded as an asserted cause in any fact.
The planned reconstruction names two alternatives (skin grafts or local thigh flaps); neither is asserted, and the source later says there was no need for either.

Follow-up is "nearly one year" in the text and "10-month" in the Figure 6 caption. These are not two values for one stated measurement (the caption dates the photographed result; the text gives the follow-up length), so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict; both are kept as separate facts and events.

Radiotherapy "finishing one year prior to presentation to our clinic" is anchored to a clinic presentation that the source does not explicitly equate with the referral to the Plastic Surgery Division, so no relation to the referral event is recorded.

The inguinal swelling, pain, edema and erythema presentation (b00009) is not explicitly tied to the referral to Plastic Surgery (b00007) or to the six-month lymphedema history; no order or identity between these is inferred.

The only sex wording is the pronoun "She"; the article calls the patient male-to-female transgender and does not state sex assigned at birth. The pronoun reflects gender identity, so documented_sex (female) is kept review_only and only the documented gender identity is accepted.
The PET focal hypermetabolic area is only "probably" a lymph node, and the lipoblast-like cells "could be explained" by phagocytized silicone; both are hedged and kept hedged.

Discussion sentences b00021 refer literally to this patient ("Because the patient is male-to-female transgender, she considered...") and to her single operation, but carry no time; they are kept as untimed facts and are not linked to the nearly-one-year follow-up event.
Granulomas appear only in the abstract summary of the radiological findings; the body text does not describe them.
